name: softgauge: analytic soft gauges for surface texture software

conventions.units: lengths and heights in µm, material ratios in %, angles in degrees
conventions.grid: row-major; pixel (r, c) at x = c·dx, y = r·dy (row 0 first); samples are points, so n samples span (n − 1)·dx; crop/mask boxes and circles use y measured from the bottom: yb = (ny − 1 − r)·dy
conventions.judging: pass iff |value − ref| ≤ tol.abs + tol.rel·|ref|, where ref = discrete.value if present else reference.value; expectNaN cases pass iff the value is NaN/undefined
conventions.tiers: core = parameters of an unprocessed gauge; operators = standard operations measured on the array; extension = non-standard parameters, implementation-specific operations and analysis outputs

plane.title: Tilted plane
plane.description: A least-squares plane. Every height statistic of the sampled plane has a closed form (sum of two discrete uniform distributions); every finite difference is exact.

plane-iso.title: Tilted plane (isotropic)
plane-iso.description: Plane sloping along x on a square-pixel grid, used to check that rotation preserves slope magnitude and turns its direction by the requested angle.

egg.title: Centred egg-crate
egg.description: Product of cosines centred on the grid with 8 × 6 full periods. Its sampled mean is 0 and its moments are exact: Sq = A/2, Sku = 9/4.

egg+poly1.title: Egg-crate + plane
egg+poly1.description: Egg-crate plus a first-degree polynomial. Levelling must return the egg-crate exactly, because it is orthogonal to the polynomial on the sampled grid.

egg+poly2.title: Egg-crate + quadratic
egg+poly2.description: Egg-crate plus a full second-degree polynomial (with cross term).

egg+poly3.title: Egg-crate + cubic
egg+poly3.description: Egg-crate plus a full third-degree polynomial.

plane+bump.title: Plane with a bump
plane+bump.formula: z = a·x + b·y + c + h·cos²(πρ/2r₀)·[ρ < r₀]
plane+bump.description: Tilted plane carrying a cos² bump. A plane fitted only around reference points on the flat part must remove the tilt exactly and leave the bump.

step.title: Two-level step
step.formula: z = h for x < x_s, else 0
step.description: A fraction d = 1/4 of the surface at height h, the rest at 0. Its height distribution is Bernoulli, so all height parameters including skewness and kurtosis are exact.

disc.title: Disc plateau
disc.description: A sharp circular plateau. Masking the same circle must leave a perfectly flat surface. The centre is chosen so that no pixel lies exactly on the circle.

sine.title: Sinusoid
sine.description: 10 full periods sampled with P = 64 points per period (a multiple of 4, so crests and troughs are sampled). Height moments over full periods are exact.

sine-f32.title: Sinusoid (float32 storage)
sine-f32.description: The sinusoid gauge stored as 32-bit floats, the storage type of several instrument formats.

sine-acf.title: Sinusoid (ACF)
sine-acf.description: 64 periods of λ = 16 µm at 1 µm sampling. Its ACF is A²/2·cos(2πτx/λ) and does not decay along y, so Str is undefined.

sine-abbott.title: Sinusoid material-ratio curve
sine-abbott.description: The material-ratio curve of a sinusoid, h(mr) = A·cos(π·mr/100), laid out as a raster ramp of N = 20 000 heights so the sampled curve is exact. (A sampled sinusoid repeats each height many times, so its empirical curve is a staircase.) It exercises the ISO 13565-2 construction on a smooth, curved material-ratio curve.

sine-hybrid.title: Sinusoid (gradients)
sine-hybrid.description: nx − 1 = 8 full periods of cells, so every forward difference set spans whole periods: the sampled Sdq and Sdr have closed forms with the secant slope amplitude a′ = 2A·sin(π/P)/Δx.

pyramids.title: Pyramid field
pyramids.formula: z = A·[T(x/λ) + T(y/λ)], T = triangle wave
pyramids.description: Sum of two triangle waves whose kinks fall on grid lines. Every grid cell is a plane with |∂z/∂x| = |∂z/∂y| = 4A/λ, so Sdq and the triangulated area are exact.

bearing.title: Material-ratio gauge
bearing.description: Heights placed in raster order along a prescribed piecewise-linear material-ratio curve (peak, core and valley zones), so the sampled material-ratio curve equals h exactly. ISO 13565-2 / ISO 25178-2 functional and volume parameters follow in closed form.

ramp.title: Uniform ramp
ramp.description: Heights uniformly distributed on [0, 1] (raster ramp), used for material-ratio thresholding.

egg-feature.title: Egg-crate (features)
egg-feature.description: 12 × 12 complete half-period cells. Hills are the squares around the extrema with i + j even, dales the others, and saddles sit at height 0. The outer ring of cells touches the border and is excluded; the 10 × 10 interior cells hold 50 hills and 50 dales. With 15 px per half-period the zero-level saddle lines lie between pixels, so the segmentation has no ties.

egg-acf.title: Egg-crate (ACF, isotropic)
egg-acf.description: 32 × 32 periods. The normalised ACF is cos(2πτx/λ)·cos(2πτy/λ); its 0.2 contour is solved numerically from that closed form.

egg-acf-aniso.title: Egg-crate (ACF, anisotropic)
egg-acf-aniso.description: λx = 16 µm, λy = 24 µm on a grid with Δy = 1.5·Δx (16 px per period on both axes), so a mix-up between x and y would be visible.

sine-filter-4.title: Sinusoid λ = 4 µm
sine-filter-4.description: Unit sinusoid of wavelength 4 µm (integer number of periods) for measuring the amplitude transmission of filters.

sine-filter-8.title: Sinusoid λ = 8 µm
sine-filter-8.description: Unit sinusoid of wavelength 8 µm (integer number of periods) for measuring the amplitude transmission of filters.

sine-filter-16.title: Sinusoid λ = 16 µm
sine-filter-16.description: Unit sinusoid of wavelength 16 µm (integer number of periods) for measuring the amplitude transmission of filters.

sine-filter-32.title: Sinusoid λ = 32 µm
sine-filter-32.description: Unit sinusoid of wavelength 32 µm (integer number of periods) for measuring the amplitude transmission of filters.

sine-filter-64.title: Sinusoid λ = 64 µm
sine-filter-64.description: Unit sinusoid of wavelength 64 µm (integer number of periods) for measuring the amplitude transmission of filters.

dither-spiked.title: Flat surface with spikes
dither-spiked.formula: z = ε(x, y) + Σ spikes, |ε| ≤ 0.01 µm
dither-spiked.description: A flat surface with a 0.01 µm noise-like texture carrying six isolated ±20 µm spikes. If the spikes get zero weight, every output of a weighted Gaussian mean is a convex combination of texture values, so it stays within ±0.01 µm, including at the border.

sine-filter-y.title: Sinusoid along y (Δy ≠ Δx)
sine-filter-y.description: Unit sinusoid of wavelength 16 µm along y on a grid with Δy = 0.25 µm and Δx = 0.5 µm: the filter must use the y step for the y kernel.

const-holes.title: Constant with holes
const-holes.description: A constant height with two rectangular non-measured regions, one touching the border. Zero-order Gaussian regression must return c everywhere, at the border and around the holes.

sphere.title: Spherical cap
sphere.description: Cap of a sphere of radius R = 500 µm over a 200 × 200 µm field.

cylinder.title: Cylinder section
cylinder.formula: z = z_c + √(R² − d²), d = distance to the axis
cylinder.description: Cylinder of radius R = 300 µm whose horizontal axis is turned 20° from the x axis.

plane-holes.title: Plane with holes
plane-holes.formula: z = a·x + b·y + c, non-measured rectangles
plane-holes.description: Tilted plane with two interior non-measured rectangles. Linear (Delaunay) interpolation of a plane is exact.

columns-hole.title: Step edge with hole
columns-hole.formula: z = [x ≥ x_s], non-measured square across the edge
columns-hole.description: A vertical step edge with a 20 × 20 px hole centred on it (even width, so no pixel is equidistant from both sides). Nearest-neighbour filling must restore the edge exactly.

sine-spiked.title: Sinusoid with spikes
sine-spiked.description: Smooth unit sinusoid (λ = 32 µm) with six isolated spikes of 12 to 15 µm. The six spikes, and nothing else, are the outliers.

sine-profile.title: Sinusoidal profile
sine-profile.description: Profile of 10 full periods with P = 64 samples per period. The 5 sampling lengths each hold 2 full periods with sampled crests.

triangle-profile.title: Triangular profile
triangle-profile.description: Triangle wave with its kinks on samples, so every forward difference has slope magnitude exactly 4A/λ.

bearing-profile.title: Material-ratio profile
bearing-profile.description: The material-ratio gauge as a profile of N = 20 000 points.

cos+line-profile.title: Cosine on a line (profile)
cos+line-profile.description: Centred cosine with 8 full periods, which is orthogonal to every straight line on the sampled grid.

sine-filter-profile.title: Sinusoidal profile λ = 16 µm
sine-filter-profile.description: Unit sinusoidal profile for the profile Gaussian filter.

sine-spectral.title: Sinusoid (spectra)
sine-spectral.description: 16 periods of a unit sinusoid. All of its power sits at f = (±1/λ, 0).

sine-90.title: Sinusoid along y
sine-90.description: Unit sinusoid whose wave vector points along y (16 whole periods).

sine-rot.title: Diagonal sinusoid
sine-rot.description: Sinusoid with wave vector (16, 16) cycles per field, i.e. θ = 45° in the array frame (y pointing down the rows), λ = 8√2 µm. The wave vector sits exactly on a DFT bin.

gauss-bumps.title: Gaussian bumps
gauss-bumps.description: A large (h = 2 µm, s = 3 µm) and a small (h = 1 µm, s = 0.75 µm) Gaussian bump. Riemann sums of Gaussians sampled finer than s converge exponentially, so the volumes are exact to round-off.

gauss-dimple.title: Gaussian dimple
gauss-dimple.description: The large bump inverted, for the concave (void) volume.

boss.title: Circular boss
boss.description: Cylindrical boss with a smooth (tanh) edge whose steepest point lies exactly on ρ = R.

edge.title: Straight edge
edge.description: Straight step edge turned by 25°, with its steepest point on the line d = 0.

plane-sample.title: Tilted plane (sampling)
plane-sample.description: Bilinear interpolation of a plane is exact at any point.

pockets.title: Pocket array
pockets.description: Six flat-bottomed rectangular pockets of depth 5 µm in a flat top surface. The edges lie halfway between pixel centres, so the 50 %-depth edge positions are exact.

pockets-dither.title: Pocket array (dithered)
pockets-dither.description: The pocket array with a 0.1 nm noise-like texture (incommensurate sinusoids), as any real measurement has: the cavity detector estimates its threshold from the top-surface noise.

bearing-cubic.title: Cubic material-ratio gauge
bearing-cubic.description: The smooth material-ratio curve of Todhunter et al. (2019, eq. 1) with Z = 1 µm, laid out as a ramp of N = 20 000 heights so that the sampled curve is exact. Unlike the curve of a sinusoid its flattest 40 % window is unique (30–70 %), so the whole ISO 13565-2 construction is defined. The closed-form values reproduce the mathematical values published in that paper (Table 1) to every printed digit.

bearing-cubic-serpentine.title: Cubic material-ratio gauge, alternate rows reversed
bearing-cubic-serpentine.formula: the cubic gauge with every odd row reversed
bearing-cubic-serpentine.description: The heights of the cubic material-ratio gauge with every second row reversed (Todhunter et al. 2019, §5.1). The height distribution, and so every material-ratio parameter, is unchanged.

bearing-cubic-scramble.title: Cubic material-ratio gauge, scrambled
bearing-cubic-scramble.formula: pixel k carries ramp sample 7919·k mod N
bearing-cubic-scramble.description: The heights of the cubic material-ratio gauge in a scrambled order (pixel k carries ramp sample 7919·k mod N, a permutation because 7919 and N are coprime), the counterpart of the random order in Todhunter et al. (2019, §5.1). No two neighbours are close in height, yet every material-ratio parameter is unchanged.

plane-A4-B3.title: Plane A = 4, B = 3
plane-A4-B3.description: Parametric plane of Todhunter et al. (2020, §4.4) with slopes A = 4, B = 3. Steep planes catch area algorithms that assume small slopes. Its area ratio is √(1 + A² + B²) − 1; the reference given in that paper, √(1 + A²)·√(1 + B²) − 1 (eq. 35), is the area of a rectangle and holds only when A·B = 0 (here it reads 1203.8 % instead of 409.90 %).

fourier-filter.title: Oblique Fourier series
fourier-filter.description: Five oblique sinusoids with integer numbers of cycles over the field (Todhunter et al. 2018, eq. 1), wavelengths 16.00, 14.31, 7.16, 2.97, 45.25 µm. A Gaussian filter must scale every term by its own transmission, which also tests the phase, the separable x/y implementation and the absence of cross-talk between terms.

egg-filter-border.title: Reflection-symmetric egg-crate
egg-filter-border.description: Egg-crate with whole half-periods across the field (16 along x, 10 along y) and its extrema half a pixel outside every border. It is unchanged by the half-sample reflection at each border, so a Gaussian filter with reflect extension must return T(λx)·T(λy)·z everywhere, including at the border, where Todhunter et al. (2020) found the largest software deviations.
